elements.evidence: grants to Client and its affiliates designated by written notice

elements.element: Licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf
elements.evidence: grant names only "Client and its affiliates designated by written notice"; no contractor coverage
grant states only "a non-exclusive license to use the Interface" with no perpetual/irrevocable language

elements.element: Subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach
elements.evidence: no termination-standard language added to the licence grant
or for an assignment by Client to a successor in a merger or acquisition
grants to Client and its affiliates designated by written notice

elements.element: Transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction
elements.evidence: no such approval shall be required ... for an assignment by Client to a successor in a merger or acquisition

reasons: Both fallback atomic elements are met: affiliates are brought within the grant conditioned on written notice, and Client may assign to an M&A successor without the counterparty's approval.

Edits are surgical — a short insertion in the grant sentence and a short exception appended to the assignment clause — with no preferred-only scope (contractors, perpetuity, irrevocability, breach-only termination) imported and no whole-clause rewrite.

Untouched commercial terms (ordinary-course field of use, Client's freedom to use alternative systems, the mutual consent requirement, the existing affiliate assignment exception) remain effective; no undefined terms or dangling mechanics introduced.
The M&A assignment exception is one-directional (Client only), which benefits our party and is not an intent problem.
